findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

A food handler was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and they were instructed to review hand washing procedures with all food handlers in the facility. Ensure that a clean barrier is used to turn off the faucet after hand washing in order to protect the freshly washed hands from re-contamination.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The ice scoop in the bar area was observed with the scoop handle in contact with the ice. This allows for bare hand contact with the Ready-To-Eat (RTE) food (ice) when picking it up. The PIC was notified and moved the scoop to correct. Ensure that all RTE foods are protected from bare hand contact at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

On arrival the inspector observed a box on top of the kitchen hand sink. The box was removed to correct. Ensure that the hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation (C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen is observed with a concentration of 0 ppm CL. The PIC was shown and had the bucket remade to correct. They also stated that the bucket was likely from lunch service and had not been changed since this morning. Ensure that all sanitizers in the facility are changed when needed so that they are maintained at effective concentration.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

1) The left side of the mop sink has a gap forming and needs to be resealed to the wall. 2) The baseboard/coving to the right of the three part sink are observed pulling away from the wall. Re-seal to the wall. Both locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair/reseal prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms (1-5).

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. This recontaminated the freshly washed hands. The PIC was notified and instructed to review hand washing with all food handlers. Ensure safe hand washing procedures take place at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The fry slicer is observed with dried on food debris along the blades. The kitchen manager was shown and had the equipment disassembled and moved to dish to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned regularly and maintained clean between uses.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

There is not a CFPM available at the facility during this inspection. Information for the local CFPM courses will be sent in an email to the facility in the morning. Ensure that a CFPM is available at the facility at all times of operation.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival only a single signed reporting agreement is available at the facility. A fresh copy was observed in the public health binder. This was used to make multiple copies that were signed by all staff prior to the inspector leaving. Violation corrected.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

A knife is observed on the shelf above the center prep cooler with a personal phone making contact with the blade. The PIC was shown and the knife moved to dish for cleaning to correct. The observed location of the phone was acceptable in general, but if it’s located there food contact items cannot be stored in that corner as well. Ensure food contact surfaces are washed and maintained clean prior to use in the facility.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

All observed food handler cards in the facility are expired at this time. The PIC is instructed to have all employees that handle food or food contact surfaces to complete food handler training and maintain a copy at the facility for verification.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

There is not a current allergen certification available at the facility at the time of this inspection. Hand outs will be sent to the PIC via email tomorrow for information purposes. Ensure that each certified food protection manager has a completed and up-to-date allergen certification. Keep copies of these certificates at the facility at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  


An employee was observed to change tasks and don gloves without hand washing. Education conducted. The PIC is instructed to ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that it is required.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the bar area is without paper towels at the beginning of the inspection. Paper towels were supplied during this inspection to correct. Ensure that paper towels are at each hand sink at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

The hand sink in the bar has multiple items in it that would prevent effective hand washing from taking place. The bartender and PIC were consulted and the items removed to correct. Ensure that the hand sinks are only used for hand washing and are easily accessible at all times.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). 

Multiple containers of food throughout the facility are observed without accurate date markings. Per the PIC they were prepared either yesterday or today depending on the items. New date markings were added during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS items held more than a day after opening/preparation are accurately date marked at all times.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. 

Containers of white powders are observed in the dry storage area without labels indicating what they contain. A conversation with the PIC revealed that they were containers of Pinko and Baking Powder. Education was conducted and labels added during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all containers of food not in their original containers are labeled moving forward.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form).

The container for the ice scoop above the ice machine is soiled with dust and a cardboard piece. The container was discussed and cleaned during the inspection to correct. Ensure that in-use utensils are stored in containers free from contaminants at all times.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

Buckets of utensils above the three part sink are soiled and in need of cleaning. The containers as well as the utensils were moved to dish and cleaned during this inception to correct. Ensure that containers used to store utensils prior to use are maintained clean in order to protect the food contact surfaces from contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

1) Food debris is observed under the cart behind the three part sinks. 2) Encrusted debris is observed on the floor around the wheels of the cart behind the three part sink. 3) Dust is accumulating on the fan cover on the walk in cooler condenser as well as the piping behind it. 4) The wall and caulking above the dish machine counter is beginning to accumulated a black substance. Clean these areas and maintain the facility clean at all times moving foreword. 

There is currently a plastic cover over the top of the three part sink. This item is observed to have an oily residue underneath it and is difficult to clean. It is highly suggested that this is removed moving foreword and the wall/sink junction is sealed directly. At the very least this location must be maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) The coving at the wall/ floor junction behind the three part sink and behind the ice machine need to be re-sealed to the wall so that the current gaps are removed. 2) There is a small hole in the wall to the right of the ice machine and under the counter that needs to be filled. 3) Where the dish machine counter metes the wall has sections where the caulking appears to have worn away or been removed. Replace the caulking to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 4) Black tape is being used to hold the order ticket holder above the prep cooler to the shelf. Tape is not a safe items to use around moisture/food. Repair the equipment using materials that can be maintained smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The fry slicer has food remnants on the blades that have been there long enough to become hard. Food contact sections of equipment should be cleaned whenever they have been contaminated and maintained clean until their next use. The item was disassembled and cleaned during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The CFPM for this facility does not have an accredited Allergen Certification at the time of this inspection. Education conducted and they are aware that they should complete it prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

1) A pair of charging headphones are stored on top of a cleaned plate on a prep cooler. 2) A marker is observed on top of plates used for calamari. Both items were discussed with the PIC. The contaminated plates were moved to dish and the items noted moved to correct the violation. Ensure that all food contact items are not exposed to possible contamination prior to use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The inner corner of the lid for the ice machine is cracked and in need of repair. Caulking was discussed as a possibility, but tape should not be used. Repair prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The three part sink in the bar area is observed with sanitizer at approximately 50 ppm Quat. Bottle directions indicate a solution of 200-400 ppm required for effective sanitizing. As the solution had just been made and not yet used more tablets were added to bring the solution up to an effective concentration and correct the violation.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Two separate moist cloths were observed on counters in the kitchen area. PIC was consulted and instructed to store these cloths in the sanitizer solution between uses. Cloths were placed back into their buckets to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Facility uses both CL and Quat based sanitizers. Only CL test strips are available at the start of the inspection. PIC and owner both were consulted and instructed to ensure that test strips are available for all sanitizers used in the facility. A small amount were acquired during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
-Fry slicer observed soiled with food debris accumulation. CORRECTED- Removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Maintain clean to sight and touch.
-Clean equipment observed in containers soiled with dust and food debris in the dry storage area. CORRECTED- Items and bins removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Sauce observed dated 9/16. Other items in prep cooler observed without dates or more than 7 days past their date-markings. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and provided education. Staff voluntarily discarded foods 7 days or more past their date markings. See General Comments for additional information.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
ROP fish observed thawing under refrigeration with a label indicating to remove from packaging prior to thawing. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who pierced packaging of barely-thawed ROP fish.
3-501.13: (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Food debris and spills observed on the floor in the dry storage area (under shelving and in the corner between freezers). Clean as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed a cell phone and a pack of cigarettes stored on the counter near the prep coolers. Store personal items away from food prep areas. CORRECTED-- Items relocated to appropriate storage away from food.
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employees wash hands, use clean hands to dispense paper towels, then use paper towel to turn the faucet off. This potentially recontaminates hands. Dispense paper towels prior to washing or use an elbow or other barrier to dispense paper towels to prevent contamination of clean hands. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC and provided education.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Coving observed to be pushed in, exposing gap between kitchen tile and wall. Repair/replace coving to seal floor/wall gap.
6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Foods observed throughout the kitchen without date markings. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Facility is open Tuesday through Saturday (closed Sunday and Monday). Foods are not kept from one week to the next, so unlabelled foods were prepared yesterday (Tuesday). PIC will label foods with the dates they were prepared if they will be held for more than 24 hours.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Staff observed leaving kitchen, returning, and continuing food prep without washing hands or changing gloves. After any activity that may have contaminated hands (like leaving the kitchen), employees must wash hands and change gloves before returning to food preparations. CORRECTED-- Provided education.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Accumulation of debris observed in grout and around floor drains in the kitchen. Clean floors to preclude accumulation of debris. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed keys, a cell phone, and a bag of cigarettes stored on the counter near the prep cooler and oven/grill. Store personal items away from food prep areas. CORRECTED-- Items relocated to appropriate storage away from food.
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
(REPEAT #2) CFM has not completed ANSI-approved allergen training. Ensure all CFMs take ANSI-approved allergen training.
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
(REPEAT 1) No CFMs have completed ANSI-approved allergen training. Ensure all CFMs take ANSI-approved allergen training.
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency. (C)

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
No CFMs have completed ANSI-approved allergen training. Ensure all CFMs take ANSI-approved allergen training.
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency. (C)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed bar sink to not have running hot water. PIC stated that a plumber will be called to remedy the problem.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 38oC (100oF) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. (Pf)

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment: Observed container of sugar without name label. CORRECTED- Employee provided a label at time of inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. (C)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed bar wiping cloth on counter out of solution. CORRECTED- Wiping cloth was placed in sanitizer.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14 (B) (1) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. (C) •

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed the saute and pantry coolers to be out of temperature. The saute cooler had products probed with internal temperatures ranging from 46F-52F. The pantry cooler had products probed with internal temperatures from 46F-50F. The facility contacted HVAC immediately for repair. They discovered the coils on the machines were no longer clean and causing the machines to overheat. The facility voluntarily discarded all products from both coolers. 
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed multiple PHFs in a cooler that was all above 50F. When the air temperature was checked, the cooler was noted to be at 54F. Ensure that PHFs are maintained below 41F when being cold held. Facility called HVAC while inspector was in the facility and cleaned the coils to the cooler. All PHFs were discarded. 2) Observed hummus and salad dressing in the cooler by the bar without date marking. Chef states that the hummus was made yesterday and the dressing would've been made Sunday at the latest. Ensure that all PHFs are properly date marked. Items were date marked during the inspection. 
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
1) Observed an employee drink on top of the dish machine without a lid or a straw. Drinks should be provided with a lid and a straw and stored below and away from food/food surfaces. 2) Observed personal ice cream being stored in the reach-in freezer in the back area. Ensure that personal food is stored below and away from food for service. 
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed a personal water bottle in the chest freezer, that had the seal broken, being stored on top of food for service. Ensure that personal drinks are provided with a lid and a straw, as well as stored below and away from food. Drink removed from the freezer during the inspection. 
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Observed miso in the cooler that was dated from December of last year. There was mold growing around the lid of the container. Ensure that food is discarded when it is no longer in a safe condition. The container was discarded during the inspection. 
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed dressing in the double door cooler that was dated for 07/26. The dressing is a vinagerette that is made in house. This is past the allowed 7 days and should have already been discarded. Bartender discarded the dressing during the inspection. 2) Observed the sushi cooler to be extremely out of temperature. The chef stated that one of his employees had just finished detailing the inside, but he had detailed it while the food was in the cooler. This allowed all of the food within the cooler to rise to 60-65F when probed. After talking with the chef, he agreed to discard the food by 8 PM, since the employee had started cleaning the cooler at 4 PM. Ensure that, when cleaning cold holding units, it is done when the unit does not contain PHFs and give the cooler adequate time to come back into temperature. 
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed clean dishes in the rear of the facility that had dried crumbs accumulated on them. There was no food storage noted in the immediate, surrounding area of the dishes so it is unsure as to the source. The chef removed all of the contaminated dishes and placed them in the dish area to be rewashed. Ensure that clean equipment and utensils are stored in a manner that protects from contamination. 
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the three compartment sink at the bar to have a leak around the top of the faucet. The chef states that a plumber was just out and made repairs to the sink, but he would contact him again. There was also a build up of calcification noted around where the leak was occurring. Ensure that the calcification is removed and that the faucet is maintained in good repair without leaks.

750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.
Observed that the chest freezer in the store room did not contain a thermometer. Provide thermometers in all refrigeration units.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.
Observed that the scoops for flour and panko in the dry storage bins had fallen into the product. Handles should be extended out of product to minimize hand contact with food.
CORRECTED= handles were extended out of product.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
Observed that the lid of the chest freezer in the store room was damaged. Repair or replace lid or unit so as to be easily maintained and clean.(**Repeat violation**) 
Observed that the door gaskets of the prep cooler on the north ( right side) in prep area were damaged. Repair gaskets so as to be free of crevices and easily maintained. 
Observed that the shelves inside the antique bar are raw wood surfaces. Seal these surfaces so as to be easily cleanable.(**Repeat violation**)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Observed that some of the shelves in the store room had some spillage. Observed that the drain pipe from wine ice bin cooler is rusty and soiled(**Repeat violation**). Observed that the catch tray underneath the broiler was soiled. CORRECTED= tray was removed and cleaned.
Clean / repair the above-referenced areas as necessary.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled that protects them from contamination.
Observed cleaned utensils stored in a tray in the kitchen near the dish area that were uncovered or unprotected. Cover or wrap clean silverware to avoid potential contamination.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.
Observed that the floors in the following areas were either soiled or in need of repairs: 1) store room, especially under shelving units, was soiled, 2) the floor of the walk in cooler is rusty and/or damaged(**Repeat violation**), 3) under the ice bin in the bar has food debris, and 4) under the equipment in the wait station is dusty (**Repeat violation**). 
Clean the floors, and repaint or repair those areas as necessary.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
Observed that the walls and/or attached equipment were in need of cleaning or repairs in the following areas: 1) the caulk around the base of the mopsink, 2) the coving along the wall=(a) behind the hand sink in the kitchen and (b) behind the chest freezer and water heater in the store room, has become detached from the wall, 3) next to the chest freezer is an old outlet that has no cover over it, 4) there is a gap between the drywall and the electrical panel in the store room, and 5) the base of the 3 compartment sink ( around the drain pipes) is soiled. 
Clean / repair these above-referenced areas as necessary.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed no dates on lobster bisque, vanilla bean burry blanc and baked potatoes.  Items were labeled with dates as to when they were prepared during the inspection.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed scoops laying in the ice, flour and sugar.  Scoops must be extended out of the food.  Extend handles out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1. (REPEAT)  Observed bare wood shelves in the bar area underneath the liquor bottles.  Paint the shelves to make a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 2.Observed the left gasket on the south prep cooler to be broken.  Replace the gasket. 3. The chest freezer in the dry storage area needs defrosted.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1. Piece that water drains through from wine trough is soiled. 2.  Underneath the broiler (where debris falls) is soiled.  Clean these items.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed silverware stored uncovered on tables.  Clean utensils should be protected from potential cross contamination.  Properly store clean utensils and glassware.
750-870 Tableware may be set prior to serving a meal when glasses and cups are inverted, and knives, forks and spoons are wrapped or otherwise covered.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the base of the three compartment sink faucet.  Repair the leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the following floors to be soiled or in disrepair: 1. (REPEAT) Walk in cooler floor is rusty. 2. (REPEAT)x3 Tiles below ice bin at bar are peeling up.  Replace tiles. 3. (REPEAT) South side of the bar where the tile meets the carpet has duct tape.  4. Corners of the kitchen have debris buildup. 5.  The drain located in the first door in bar area. 6. Floor underneath the dish machine where chemicals are stored. 7. Floor in bar area where carpet meets the tile is soiled on north side.  Clean and repair the floors.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following walls and ceilings to be soiled or in disrepair: 1. (REPEAT)x3 Paint at sides and underneath urinal was peeling and wall was damaged below urinal.  Repair the wall and repaint around the urinal.  Caulk the urinal to the wall and re-caulk the coving under urinal. 2. (REPEAT)  The wall near the bar three compartment sink has food splash.  3. (REPEAT) The wall underneath the dish machine has food splash and black buildup.  4. Dish machine area that has black buildup where the wall and floor meet.  Clean the walls and ceilings.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a chemical bottle unlabeled during the inspection.   Label the chemical bottle with the proper common name.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed a mop stored in dirty water.  Mops should be hung in a way for them to dry in between uses.  Properly store the mops and empty water at the end of the night.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No food handler was present during the beginning of the inspection.  A certified food handler must be present at all times for Class I High Risk facilities.   A food handler was present at the end of the inspection.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Found 7-10 tomatoes to be moldy in the walk-in cooler storage box. Cook discarded the tomatoes during the inspection.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed a powder unlabeled in the dry storage area on top of a rice container. Label the bin with its proper common name.
750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name;, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Dish machine tested at 0 ppm Chlorine. Inspector primed the machine and after was tested at 50 ppm Chlorine. Violation was corrected, make sure dish machine reaches 50-100 ppm Chlorine.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed a metal spoon utensil to have food debris on it.  All food contact surfaces must be properly wash, rinsed and sanitized.Clean the utensil.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: 1.REPEAT inside oven 2. REPEAT metal spice rack 3. REPEAT dry storage shelves 4. REPEAT ledge below compressor inside the prep coolers 5. Shelves were pans are stored underneath the microwave in the dry storage next to the water heater.Clean these areas.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed to-go containers on the floor of the dry storage area.  Single service items should be stored at least 6" off the floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the base of the spray hose next to dish machine. Repair the leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed mouse droppings around the water heater and near the rice rack.  Terminix is coming tomorrow to treat for rodents. Mouse droppings are to be cleaned up in order to show mouse control is working.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the screen door in the back of the facility to have gaps along the top and in the right corner of door. Outer openings should be tight fitting. Repair the screen door.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors were soiled: 1. REPEAT Inside the bar cabinet next to handsink (heavy buildup on floor and in drain) 2. REPEAT BAR along walls and along the cords/threshold between bar and carpet. 3. REPEAT behind the water heater (old mouse droppings) 4. REPEAT carpet with heavy buildup under small prep cooler and three door cooler across from bar.5 behind rack in storage room across from spice door 6. walk-in cooler floor is rusty. Resurface the floor. 7 REPEAT tiles below ice bin at bar were peeling up. Repair the tiles.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1. REPEAT Paint at sides and underneath urinal was peeling an wall was damaged below urinal. Repair the wall and re-paint around the urinal.
2. Observed holes above the dish machine sprayer on the wall. Seal the holes to make it a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
3. Observed coving pulling away from the wall by the prep cooler and knife holder. Re-caulk the coving.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
